label: mid-original-phase (t=3-6) input from a token set {b,j,g,m,z,0,u,2,i,1} in sequences starting with f/c/d/3/r/x/o
explanation: Fires almost only in the original phase (99.4% of mass). It is silent at t=0-2, peaks at t=4-5 (orig_idx 4 has a 5.9% rate) and is nearly gone by t>=8. It never fires in the copy phase, and fires only weakly and rarely on <DEL>. Within that window it is gated by two token identities. The first is the first original token: f, c and d give 5-6x lift and 3, r, x and o give about 3x, while l and the other first tokens are well below base rate. The second is the current input: b and j give over 4x lift, then g, m, z, 0, u, 2, i and 1 at 2-3x. It also prefers the first occurrence of the input token (in_first=1 holds 89% of mass). The strongest activations come when the second original token is also from {f,c,d,3} (e.g. f d 1 b b g ...). Requiring that raises precision to 0.65 but cuts recall sharply. Requiring only phase 0 and t=3-6 already covers 97% of activations (precision 0.04). The conjunction with the first-token and input-token sets reaches dev F1 0.55 (precision 0.43, recall 0.76, mass recall 0.84). The token sets look like a distributed lookup over several tokens rather than one clean category, so the description is incomplete.
